## TL;DR

The server handoff check exposed a test isolation bug: the standalone `repoos check` subprocess could inherit `REPOOS_REMOTE_VALIDATION_DONE=1` from a parent validation process. That flag tells the CLI remote gate it has already run, so the subprocess exited successfully instead of exercising the expected remote failure path. The test now explicitly clears that inherited flag. I verified the regression under a parent process with the flag set, then ran the full scoped RepoOS check successfully.

## Work and rationale

The queued server failure pointed to `tests/pre-review-remote-gate.test.ts` and the assertion expecting the child process to exit with status 1. The test already constructed a child environment that reset `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED` and `REPOOS_SKIP_TESTS`, but it inherited all other variables from `process.env`. The remote validation completion flag was therefore able to leak into this isolated child. This made test behavior dependent on which validation context launched it.

I added `REPOOS_REMOTE_VALIDATION_DONE` to the test's explicit environment resets and assigned it an empty value. The test imports the flag name from the existing module, avoiding a duplicated literal and keeping the setup aligned with the implementation. This keeps the test meaningful: the child CLI must run its own gate and record the unavailable-runner failure rather than silently accepting the parent process's completion state.

The change is confined to test setup. It does not alter the feature implementation or remote validation behavior in production.

## Approaches tried

I first reran the focused pre-review remote gate test suite in its ordinary environment. It passed all 31 cases, consistent with the failure being dependent on inherited process state rather than a deterministic regression. I then reran that same suite with `REPOOS_REMOTE_VALIDATION_DONE=1` set in the parent environment. With the child now clearing the flag, all 31 cases passed, including the standalone CLI test that had failed during server finalization.

After the focused reproduction, I ran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. It created a WIP checkpoint for the changed test, then ran the changed-path suite on a remote runner. Two runners were skipped because their link probes missed the configured bandwidth floor; a third runner passed the link probe and completed validation. The remote build and all 302 scoped test files passed. The contrast audit, browser/UI smoke gate, local formatting, lint, build, asset guards, and user-docs build also passed.

## Challenges and blockers

The main challenge was reproducing a failure that appeared only during server-side validation. The first ordinary focused run passed, so rerunning it without recreating the parent environment would not have established the cause. Explicitly setting the inherited completion flag reproduced the exact class of environment leak while exercising the corrected child setup.

Remote validation took longer than a local test run. The first two hosts were rejected by the runner's link probe, so the check retried on a third host. That host passed validation. There are no remaining blockers from this check.

## Key learnings

Tests that launch a second CLI process should clear every environment variable that changes the behavior under test, including orchestration markers inherited from the parent process. Clearing only the obvious check-selection variables was insufficient because the remote gate also has a completion marker. A focused test launched with that marker set is a useful regression check for this boundary.
